title: The Tidy Nature Shelf
markdown:
The morning sun, soft as warm honey, woke Mina. A quiet Saturday, perfect for the clubhouse. The nature shelf was a jumble. Leaves tumbled with shells. Little stones lay beside fluffy seeds.

Mina whispered, “A playful breeze has been here.”

Fern the fox, ears like rust-coloured leaves, came closer. Voice like rustling grass. “A tangle. My favourite shiny shell is hidden. How will we find it?”

Captain Ivo, kind leader, eyes like little stars, tapped his hands together. Warm and steady — no never-fear-little-explorers. “A puzzle for clever thinkers. Let’s make the shelf neat.”

They began to sort. Mina picked up a soft green leaf. “From a tree. Part of a plant.”

Fern nudged a smooth grey stone, then corrected himself toward a shell, nose twitching. “This was a little house for a sea creature.”

Ivo nodded. “Everything has a story. Nature’s clues.” He held out tiny round seeds. “Promise of new sprouts.”

Mina smiled. “Leaves: plant. Shell: animal. And look.” A fluffy feather. “A bird. Also animal.” She placed the leaf in one pile, the shell in another, the feather near — no, not near the fuzzy seed. The seed was a plant’s future. The feather went with the shell’s animal corner. Fern added smooth stones to their own pile, which was neither leaf nor house.

“Groups,” Fern said, tail wagging. “Smooth things. Leafy things. It makes sense.”

Ivo chuckled, soft rain. “Classifying. Alike with alike.”

Mina beamed. “A leaf corner. A shell corner. A stone corner. Easier to find.” She held up curled bark. “Plant part.”

The shelf looked wonderfully tidy. Soft leaves in one row, smooth shells in another, stones like a tiny river. Each thing a cozy place. Fern’s shiny shell sat where a fox could see it without excavating seeds.

Ivo did not call it a secret language or address dear children. He let the rows speak: look for what is shared, and you can find a shell before naptime.

Fern yawned, a wide sleepy stretch. “A lovely sort.” Eyes heavy. Mina set one last stone in the river-line, satisfied. Ivo sat beside them as the sun dipped pink and gold. They did not drift off on the page. The clubhouse kept its Saturday; the shelf, for once, could be left without a search party.
